thread:
infra-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on prod-gateway (>= 7% over baseline) — auto-pager triggered :rotating_light:
emma: seeing tons of TLS handshake failures in the gateway logs, looks like client hello -> 525 handshake_timeout / 526 handshake_failure
leo: logs look like expired intermediate in the chain? snippet:```
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z gateway[conn=12345] ERROR tls: handshake failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2026-03-15T14:12:05Z gateway[conn=12350] WARN tls: tls13 client_hello: missing extensions
```
rajesh: @emma can you confirm which cert rotated last night and whether the CA chain upload succeeded?
emma: checked vault: leaf cert renewed at 02:00, intermediate upload job returned 200 but the chain order seems wrong (intermediate + root instead of root + intermediate). i suspect some proxies picked up bad chain.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling back cert-upload to previous known-good bundle (job id: cert-upload-20260314-0200) — started job -> /ops/jobs/9876
maria: adding immediate mitigation: routing policy to divert TLS termination to backup-edge in eu-west-1 for critical customers. applying now.
cs-rep: ringing in: two paying customers reported API errors in last 10m (acct ids: C-8892, C-4421). they see repeated 502/524 when calling generate endpoints.
rajesh: oncall handoff: i'm taking lead, ping me if anything blocks. switching to bridge in 2 min.
emma: quick check: ocsp responder looked ok, ocsp stapling failing for some leaves — likely due to wrong chain ordering. re-uploading corrected chain to staging for verification.
leo: can we short-term tolerate increased latency if we route to backup-edge? that's fine for these customers if it buys time.
rajesh: do it. maria: confirm which route table change you applied.
maria: Route change: `traffic-route --prefix /v1/generate --to backup-edge-eu-west-1 --weight 1.0` (applied) — traffic shifted ~35% away from affected edges. monitoring: https://graphs.internal/teams/gateway/edges/prod
infra-bot: Incident: paging set to HIGH. Acknowledged by raesh (oncall).
rajesh: running quick probe against problematic edge:```bash
curl -v https://gateway.prod.redwood.ai/v1/health -H 'Host: api.customer'
```
emma: probe output shows handshake TLSv1.3 -> alert: `alert certificate_unknown` for a subset of clients.
leo: I can hotfix LB config to prefer server-signed chain ordering if the client accepts it — but that requires a rolling config push. ETA 8 mins.
ops-bot: started rolling LB config for edge-prod-pool-4 (batch size 3/12)
cs-rep: FYI CS is drafting customer-facing note: brief outage, routing to backup, working on cert chain fix. want ETA before broadcasting.
rajesh: break down tasks: (1) fully validate corrected chain and push to all edge TLS config (emma) (2) complete LB config roll to prefer corrected ordering (leo) (3) monitor 5xx rate and key customer errors (maria) (4) prepare incident page for customers (cs-rep).
emma: validated corrected chain in staging, no handshake failures. pushing to prod via cert-ctl: `cert-ctl apply --bundle corrected-chain.pem --targets edge-prod-*` -> started.
ops-bot: cert-ctl job queued (id 9881) -> in-progress.
leo: LB config roll finished for batch 6/12, no regressions so far.
rajesh: after cert-ctl finishes we'll force re-negotiation by restarting TLS workers on affected nodes: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/gateway-tls -n prod --selector=edge-pool=affected`
emma: cert-ctl reported success for 9/12 nodes, failing on 3 nodes with permission error to read from KMS. investigating.
leo: kicked restart on those 3 nodes manually, they picked up corrected bundle and began serving proper chain.
maria: 5xx rate down from 7% -> 1.1% over last 6 minutes. customer error rates for C-8892 dropped to 0.2%.
cs-rep: drafting update: "We mitigated service errors by routing traffic to backup edge and correcting a certificate chain ordering issue. Most customers restored within 15 minutes."
rajesh: confirming root cause: incorrect certificate chain ordering uploaded during automated renewal job resulted in some TLS stacks rejecting the chain (intermittent across clients). action items: fix upload job to validate ordering, add chain-order unit test, add rollout gating on a synthetic handshake test, improve monitoring to alert on cert-related handshake_error spikes.
emma: filed issue: infra/9642 "cert-upload: enforce root-first chain ordering + preflight handshake check" with PR queued.
ops-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated — 5xx rate back to baseline. closing in 30m unless regressions. :white_check_mark:
rajesh: handoff to next oncall @leo in 20 minutes, summarizing state in bridge notes. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
leo: will monitor for the next hour and follow up on the ticket.
infra-bot: NOTE: post-incident actions: please fill the incident template (link: /incidents/postmortem/new?incident=2113456789) and attach timelines and customer impact estimates."
